## Vibes, Scene-Setting

The trail is long and your lips are chapped dry. When you pause the only sound is the rustling of the live oaks and the shek-shek-shek of Steller's jays screaming overhead. It's one of those days that's so hot, you're pressed between two suns as the heat radiates back up out of the hard clay earth. Your feet sweat in your boots. It’s still a week to Ossadavia, to shade, and real rest in a real bed. You can almost see Fink's tea stall, the condensation on the outside of your cold glass, honey drifting in a lazy whirlpool as you stir your spoon. 

The wind blows in from the coast and you think for a second you smell smoke, but you don’t see anything on the horizon. Is your mind playing tricks again? Burn Season is still months away. The Grove Cooperative's Greenkeepers are trying to hold the line but they're stretched thin; few communities would survive without their drought-tolerant seed varietals. More precious than coin.

Solmara was once a powerful nation, now it's a spiderweb of trail-connected communities in flammable forests, manzanita-dotted chaparral, and cracked desert. Mistgate to Sana Amaris, generations after massive wildfires burned the old world to the ground, life persists in a carefully-managed cycle of burn and renewal. Arcane Sunstone, mined from beneath the earth, turns sunlight into power a town can live on. Solmara is trying again, maybe differently this time.

But Burn is coming early this year, like it has the last several years. And some of the fires smell strange. Rumors whisper of a flame unquenchable by water. No one wants to say the word, but its vibrations still hang in the blistering air: arson.

1800s California cowboy/vaquero meets post-apocalyptic solarpunk. Inspired by Station Eleven (Mandel), A Psalm for the Wild-Built (Chambers), Always Coming Home (Le Guin), and Avatar the Last Airbender (DiMartino & Konietzko). You might be a traveling musician or poet, an arcane rig-mender or a mail courier, a rancher displaced by fire or a six-shooter-wielding outlaw, a disaffected Greenkeeper or a cleric of one of the five sister goddesses.

## About the Game

**Trans-led, queer-friendly, anti-racist table.**

This is a narrative-first table just as interested in a quiet moment shared between characters or an argument over rationing as a world-changing battle. So character growth matters just as much as mechanical optimization. I'm DMing this one, with my own former DM joining as a player; both of us write for a living and love obsessing over the details of a campaign. Expect epic narrative stakes, but also room for characters to breathe.

**About You**

If you're the kind of person who finds yourself thinking about a scene days later, who cares more about who your character is becoming than what's on their sheet, and who'd genuinely enjoy helping build out the world's wiki alongside us rather than seeing it as homework—we'd love to hear from you. We know that's a big ask, but this campaign exists because we wanted a table as nerdy for narrative as we are.  
  
28+ preferred. We’re in our 30s, and we're looking for players at a similar life stage. 

Note that this world lives with real loss; societal collapse, grief, death, and what it takes to rebuild after something ends are all key themes. Wildfire and its aftermath are a recurring presence. Nothing here is meant to be grimdark for its own sake, but these themes will come up meaningfully.
